title: A Survey of Machine Learning Methods for Time Series Prediction
tldr: Comprehensive survey of 79 papers comparing tree-based and deep learning methods for time series prediction under identical experimental conditions, finding LightGBM and RNNs top-performing.
problem_and_motivation: Existing survey papers on time series prediction struggle to draw meaningful model comparisons because they analyze studies using different implementations and datasets. This heterogeneity obscures true performance differences between tree-based and deep learning approaches.
approach: Systematically searched Web of Science for papers comparing tree-based (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) and deep learning (RNN, LSTM, GRU, CNN, Transformer) methods on identical datasets.
Selected 79 influential papers published between 2017-2024 using citation-based and temporal sampling criteria.
Introduced Fractional Performance Advantage (FPA) and Weighted Rank Advantage (WRA) metrics for cross-paper comparison.
Analyzed performance by task type (classification, regression), dataset size, time interval, and research focus area.
Reviewed error metrics and hyperparameter tuning methods used across the surveyed literature.
findings: num: Tree-based methods like LightGBM deliver best overall balance of accuracy and computational efficiency.
Tree-based models achieve competitive accuracy with deep learning at a fraction of the training and inference cost.
RNN/LSTM-based deep learning models excel on large-scale, long-sequence time series data.
Dataset size and time interval significantly influence relative model performance rankings.
M5 competition winners used LightGBM; M6 winners used a mix of tree-based and neural approaches.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: RF and GBDT Architecture → Structural differences between Random Forest and Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees.
Figure 2: FFNN, CNN, and RNN Architecture → Modifications needed to transform FFNN into CNN or RNN.
Figure 2.3: Overall Model Performance FPA and WRA scores → Tree-based models lead on average across all studies.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides a structured comparison of tree-based versus deep learning methods for time series prediction, using novel FPA and WRA metrics to enable cross-paper analysis. It establishes that LightGBM and RNN/LSTM architectures are the top performers, with tree-based methods offering superior computational efficiency. The paper provides practical guidelines for model selection based on task type, dataset size, and computational constraints.
directly_justifies: Tree-based and deep learning methods both top-performing for time series prediction tasks.
LightGBM offers best accuracy-to-efficiency ratio among surveyed methods.
RNN/LSTM preferred for large-scale, long-sequence time series data.
Dataset size and time interval significantly influence optimal model choice.
limits: Survey limited to papers comparing both TBML and deep learning within same experimental setup.
Transformer-based time series methods may be underrepresented due to publication date cutoff.
Does not cover probabilistic forecasting or uncertainty quantification methods.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling and Forecasting Algorithms) was flagged as high relevance because the paper directly surveys and compares ML methods for time series prediction. All other domains (1-5, 7-14) were rejected: the paper does not address demographics, financial behavior, expense categorization, budgeting, anomaly detection, mobile UX, privacy, engagement, evaluation frameworks, savings, synthetic data, or ML serving. Borderline case: Domain 7.C (Constrained Optimization) was considered but rejected because the survey does not cover budget optimization approaches.

limitations: Survey limited to 79 papers from Web of Science, may miss relevant work from other databases.
Citation-based selection may introduce bias toward established rather than novel methods.
FPA and WRA metrics are novel and not externally validated as comparison tools.
remember_this: LightGBM and RNN/LSTM are top-performing time series prediction methods.
Tree-based methods offer competitive accuracy with significantly lower computational cost.
Model choice depends on task type, dataset size, and time interval of historical data.
FPA and WRA metrics enable direct comparison across heterogeneous experimental setups.
